title: fix(objectql, plugin-auth)!: organization delete refuses while records remain, removes its own auth structure as one unit, and never orphans a tenant column
body:
Fixes #24948
Clause-②: yes (narrowing)

Executes the maintainer's ruling on #24948 (letter B, record 6303358360), against the measurement 6297602613 and the claim 6303408016, and the seat decision 6305179819 that answered this PR's escalations (append-only ledgers exempt and kept; business units, positions, sharing rules and settings stay records; the deviations below accepted).

## What changes

**1. Refused while the organization owns records, before anything is deleted.** `POST /api/v1/auth/organization/delete` answers `409` with the standard `DELETE_RESTRICTED` code and `dependents: [{ object, count }]`, one entry per table that still names the organization in its tenant column. It carries counts only, never a row value. The refusal runs in better-auth's global `hooks.before`, ahead of the vendor handler, so a refused delete writes nothing. That includes the caller's active organization, which the vendor clears before its own `beforeDeleteOrganization` hook runs. It runs only for a caller the vendor itself would admit (a member whose role holds `organization: ['delete']`, asked of the vendor's own `hasPermission`), so a caller the vendor refuses gets the vendor's 403 and no count.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts:2440` (the `hooks.before` branch) and `:8097` (`assertOrganizationDeletable`)
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/organization-delete.ts:125` (`organizationDeleteRefusal`)

**2. The organization's own auth structure goes with it** (the exact set, measured on a booted showcase: a door-created organization owns 1 `sys_member`, 1 `sys_team`, 1 `sys_team_member`, 1 `sys_user_permission_set` and nothing else, plus the creator's session's `active_organization_id`, which is not a tenant column):

| Table | How it names the organization | Removed by |
|---|---|---|
| `sys_member` | `organization_id`, `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-member.object.ts:312` | better-auth `adapter.deleteOrganization` (better-auth 1.7.3 `dist/plugins/organization/adapter.mjs:370-395`) |
| `sys_invitation` | `organization_id`, `sys-invitation.object.ts:255` | better-auth, same call |
| `sys_team` (the default team: `teams: { enabled: true }`, `auth-manager.ts:3557`; created by better-auth `routes/crud-org.mjs:106-126`) | `organization_id`, `sys-team.object.ts:133` | plugin-auth `removeOrganizationAuthStructure`, `organization-delete.ts:204`, called from `beforeDeleteOrganization`, `auth-manager.ts:3883` |
| `sys_team_member` | only through `team_id`, `sys-team-member.object.ts:135` | same, deleted by team before the teams (`organization-delete.ts:210`) |
| `sys_user_permission_set`, **only** grants of `organization_admin` / `organization_admin_no_bypass` | `organization_id`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts:110` | same (`organization-delete.ts:219`). plugin-security's member-delete reconcile (`auto-org-admin-grant.ts:16`) did NOT remove them in time on a booted showcase, so they are removed explicitly. Every other grant scoped to the organization counts as a record. |

The exclusion list is `ORGANIZATION_AUTH_STRUCTURE`, `organization-delete.ts:85`.

**Append-only ledgers are neither records nor structure** (seat decision 6305179819). Objects declared `managedBy: 'append-only'` are left out of both refusals, and their rows are **kept**: their `organization_id` goes on naming the deleted organization, never NULL (D1) and never deleted (§8). The set is read from that existing declaration, never from a list of names (`ObjectQL.isAppendOnlyLedger`, `engine.ts:20010`). It covers the two the decision names, `sys_activity` (`packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-activity.object.ts:25`) and `sys_email` (`packages/platform-objects/src/audit/sys-email.object.ts:27`). The same declaration also covers seven more history tables, all of the same kind: `sys_audit_log`, `sys_identity_email`, `sys_job_run`, `sys_metadata_audit`, `sys_approval_action`, `sys_presence` and the platform-settings audit. Everything else that names the organization counts as a record: business units, positions, sharing rules and organization-level settings included.

**3. Atomic.** `/organization/delete` now runs through the same request-level unit of work as subject erasure (`auth-manager.ts:6717`): one engine transaction around the whole vendor request, rolled back on any 4xx/5xx answer. What it guarantees: on a driver with transactions (SQLite and the SQL drivers), everything goes or nothing does. On a driver without `beginTransaction`, the engine warns once (ADR-0119 D1) and runs without rollback. There the guarantee is the refusal in step 1, because it runs before the first write; the residual window is a record inserted between that read and the delete, which the engine refusal in step 4 then refuses after members and invitations are gone.

**4. The engine never sets a tenant column to NULL.** In `cascadeDeleteRelations`, a `sys_organization` delete first reads every relation whose field is the child's tenant column (`resolveTenantFieldName`, injected or declared, as the identity tables declare theirs) and resolves to `set_null`. It refuses with `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED` and the same `dependents` list if any row outside the cascade set names the organization, before the walk cascades or clears anything. Those relations are then skipped by the walk. An authored `cascade` / `restrict` keeps its meaning, and other lookups to `sys_organization` (a session's active organization, a parent organization) are cleared as before.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts:19602` (the call), `:19614` (the skip), `:19981` (`isTenantColumnSetNull`), `:20010` (`isAppendOnlyLedger`), `:20034` (`refuseOrganizationDeleteWhileOwned`), `:20102` (`organizationOwnedRowCounts`, the count the door asks). Nothing in `packages/spec` changes; `TENANT_SCOPE_FIELD_DEF` carries no `deleteBehavior`.

**5. The Default Organization** is not judged by the refusal. That is the last-administrator guard's reading of the anchor: `slug = 'default'`, else the only organization, on a non-walled posture only (`isDefaultOrganizationTarget`, `organization-delete.ts:180`). Its structure is not removed either. The guard answers it as before, and now with nothing changed behind the answer (see the measurements).

### The wire code: `DELETE_RESTRICTED`, not a new `ORGANIZATION_NOT_EMPTY`

A new code needs a row in `packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`, outside this card's file surface. The ledger's admission gate also refuses a registered code that re-spells a standard member, and this condition is the standard catalog's `DELETE_RESTRICTED` ("cannot delete due to dependencies", 409), which the engine's own `restrict` refusal already answers. The per-table list rides beside it as `dependents`.

## Measurements

**Main baseline** (`e4d604efd`, showcase `single`, Default Organization delete by its sole admin): `403`, but `sys_member` went 1→0 before the refusal landed: a partial delete.

**This branch, booted showcase on SQLite** (`posture-only`, the dogfood pins):
- an organization with records: `409`, `dependents` = `showcase_category (2)`, `showcase_preference (1)`. Every count before = after, the caller's active organization unchanged, no row orphaned to NULL.
- an empty door-created organization (member, admin member, invitation, default team, team member, org-admin grant): `200`, every count 0, no orphan.
- direct engine delete of the organization with records: `409 DELETE_RESTRICTED`, nothing changed.
- the operator's remedy: delete the records, then the delete answers `200` and every count is 0.
- (`single` boot) Default Organization: `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, members, teams and organization row unchanged.

**The 18.x upgrade fixtures**, after the decision (walled boot over each, `AuditPlugin` composed as `bootFixture` composes it). Three door-created organizations per fixture: untouched; holding one `sys_business_unit`; holding one record.

| Fixture | `sys_team.organization_id` NOT NULL | Untouched organization | With a business unit | With a record |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ceremonied 18.0 (`fixture-18.0` after `os migrate organization-ownership --apply`, complete, 0 blocking) | yes | `200`; organization, members, invitations, teams, team members and grants all 0; `sys_activity` naming it 4 → 7 (kept, plus the delete's own), 0 NULL | `409` `sys_business_unit (1)`, every count unchanged | `409` `showcase_category (1)`, every count unchanged |
| `fixture-18.0.0` | no (nullable) | the same: `200`, every count 0, `sys_activity` 4 → 7, 0 NULL | the same | the same |

Before the decision, the untouched organization was refused on both fixtures for its own `sys_activity (4)`, and again for `(3)` after those were deleted by hand: the delete writes activity rows itself.

**Nothing treats an `organization_id` naming a deleted organization as an error** (the decision's evidence item), measured on the ceremonied fixture after the delete:
- the ceremony's post-check: `os migrate organization-ownership --apply` re-run over that database reports `complete: true`, `blocking: 0`. It holds only `organization_id IS NULL` rows against certification (`packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-apply.ts`, the attribution and post-check `IS NULL` predicates);
- the boot guard: HEAD boots that database through `OrganizationOwnershipBootGuardPlugin`. The guard decides on one field of the ceremony's `sys_migration` marker and reads no tenant value (`packages/runtime/src/organization-ownership-boot-guard.ts`, header);
- `check:tenant-audit-census`: a static count of write call sites in source, never data. Exit 0 on this head;
- read paths: `GET /api/v1/data/sys_activity?organization_id=` with the deleted id answers `200` (tenant scoping shows the platform admin none of them, as the decision says: no organization's rows). The one reader that will see such a row is the lifecycle sweep's dangling-reference audit (`packages/objectql/src/integrity/dangling-reference-audit.ts`). It is report-only by design ("Reports; never rewrites"): its finding lands in the sweep report's `danglingReferences`, which nothing logs, refuses on or writes from (`lifecycle-service.ts`, `auditReferences`).

**R1** fresh `pnpm dev -- --fresh` (showcase, `single`): health `200`, seeded-admin sign-in `200`, 0 error lines. Default Organization delete: `403`, members 3→3, records 14→14.
**R2** `upgrade-18x-harness.dogfood.test.ts`: 12/12, both legs.
**R3/R4** walled `os dev` (`OS_TENANCY_POSTURE=isolated`, `OS_PLATFORM_OWNER_EMAIL`, `OS_AUTH_MEMBERSHIP_POLICY=invite-only`) from a scratch copy of the showcase declaring `@objectstack/organizations` (RUNNER.md recipe), re-copied from this head: `Organizations`, `Security` and `Audit` mounted, health `200`, sign-in `200`, 0 error lines.
- On that composition every door-created organization receives the showcase's per-organization seed replay, so none is untouched there. A fresh one answers `409` naming 19 tables and 132 rows, every count unchanged.
- The operator's remedy (its records deleted over `DELETE /api/v1/data/...`, three passes for ordering): the delete then answers `200` with organization, members, teams and grants 0.
- Read from the telemetry database: **310 `sys_activity` rows still name the deleted organization, 0 NULL**.

## Decisions taken (seat decision 6305179819, answering this PR's escalations)

1. **Append-only ledgers**: exempt from both refusals, rows kept, named by the declaration `managedBy: 'append-only'` (above).
2. **Business units, positions, sharing rules, organization-level settings**: records, counted; pinned refusing (dogfood and both fixtures). A door-created organization has none at birth (measured), so counting them never blocks an untouched one.
3. **Accepted deviations**:
   - the `minor` bump (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs` grades a declared narrowing `minor` during the launch window; the release that consumes it is the maintainer's call);
   - `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` (the 409 body gains `dependents`; `ObjectQL.organizationOwnedRowCounts` is new);
   - the standard `DELETE_RESTRICTED` code;
   - the generator-written files below.

## File surface

Inside the claim: `packages/objectql/src/**`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/**`, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/**`, one changeset. **Outside it, accepted by the seat for generated artefacts only:** three files that gates regenerate, each written by its generator:
- `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx` and `docs/audits/2026-08-tenant-audit-write-call-sites.counts.md` (commit `037461e5`): `check:tenant-audit-census` counts every engine write call site under `packages/plugins`, and the three deletes in `removeOrganizationAuthStructure` move it from 233 to 236. Regenerated with `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`, and the page's census-derived prose numbers restated to match.
- `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` (+5 lines): `check:engine-double-contract` pins the new test double, via `--write`.

No `packages/spec/src/**`, no `docs/adr/**`, no governed surface (`check-governed-merges`: 0 of 13 paths).

## Tests

The new test files and the edits to existing ones:
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-organization-delete-refusal.test.ts`, new (d): the refusal, every table with its count, nothing written, a declared `set_null` tenant column refused too. Controls: an empty organization deletes and a non-tenant lookup is still cleared; a never-provisioned table refuses nothing; and `organizationOwnedRowCounts`. The append-only ledger: an organization only a ledger names deletes, and the ledger rows are kept naming it, with no write to the ledger. Beside a ledger, a record still refuses and only the record is named; and the count never includes a ledger.
- `packages/objectql/src/federated-injected-column-readers.test.ts`, edited: rows for the two new tenant-column readers, and the enumerated set of skipping sites gains `organizationOwnedRowCounts`.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/organization-delete.test.ts`, new: what counts, NULL-named grants included; the 409 body; the Default Organization reading (walled: none); the structure removal's order and reach.
- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/organization-delete-refuse-nonempty.dogfood.test.ts`, new, booted with the `AuditPlugin` composed: (a) (b) (c) (d), the vendor-refused caller (no count), and the remedy. In (b), every `sys_activity` row naming the organization before the delete is still there after it, none NULL. Also an organization holding only a business unit: `409` with `sys_business_unit (1)`, nothing changed.
- `organization-delete-federated-fixture.dogfood.test.ts`, edited: the delete now also asserts nothing names the organization afterwards. Added: (e) the Default Organization 403 with every row unchanged; and a 409 refusal on the same federated deployment, proving the count skips the federated injected anchor too.
- `org-record-admin-reach.dogfood.test.ts`, edited: the doomed door-created organization's default team, team member and grants are gone after the 200, with no orphan. Control: the same owner's delete of an organization holding a record is refused 409 with its count, members unchanged. No assertion was weakened.

**Ablations** (one-shot, `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, restored to HEAD's blob):
- engine: replacing the `refuseOrganizationDeleteWhileOwned` call: the 3 refusal pins red, the 4 controls green.
- plugin-auth gate: inverting `owned.length > 0` (rebuilt, `ablation-dist-preflight` marker present in `dist`): (a) red. Notably the status stayed `409` and the rows unchanged: the engine refusal plus the request transaction still held. Only the door's `dependents` list was gone. Restore leg rebuilt, marker absent.
- A first gate attempt that deleted the call was a no-op (the DTS build refused the now-unused method), so it ran nothing.
